script.text: Good morning! I'm Kelly, and this is your daily lesson for August 24. Today we're exploring two powerful ideas together.
Imagine a bank account where you spend more than you earn.  Eventually, you're broke.  Now imagine that with forests, fisheries, energy, even your own health.

Every resource has a regeneration rate. Forests regrow at certain speeds. Energy can be renewed. Even personal energy replenishes. Sustainability means matching consumption to regeneration. Unsustainable practices don't fail immediately—consequences lag.  This makes it easy to ignore them.
Today's wisdom: Here's today's wisdom: You can't draw from a well forever if you take more than it refills.  Match consumption to regeneration—in resources and in life.
Now let's take what we learned and put it into practice.
Today's growth challenge is Sustainability Check - Consumption vs Regeneration.

Here's your activity: Pick a resource you depend on: energy, time, money, relationships, health. Are you consuming faster than it regenerates? What would sustainable look like? Sometimes small reductions in consumption, combined with investment in regeneration, transform unsustainable patterns. This helps you audit personal resource sustainability.
And here's how today's lessons connect: What you learned about living without using up can be applied to sustainability check - consumption vs regeneration. Practice makes progress.
That's today's lesson. Learn something, grow a little. I'll see you tomorrow with something new. Stay curious!
